title: HeMeR: Heterogeneous Memory Reconciliation for Embodied Agents via Structured KV Reuse
abstract: arXiv:2611.16487v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Embodied agents make decisions by combining information from heterogeneous memory modules, including declarative memory for explicit knowledge, procedural memory for learned routines, and working memory for current observations. During interaction, the memory contents required for decision making change with the agent's state, goal, and task progress, while many contents remain shared across consecutive decisions. However, existing memory modules are typically accessed through separate interfaces, so each updated memory context is often processed as a new input to the foundation model. This prevents selective key-value (KV) cache reuse for unchanged memory contents and forces full KV cache recomputation even when much of the memory context remains valid. translated_title: HeMeR：基于结构化KV复用的具身智能体异构记忆协调框架
translated_abstract: 具身智能体通过组合来自异构记忆模块的信息进行决策，这些模块包括存储显性知识的声明性记忆、存储已学习例程的程序性记忆，以及存储当前观察的工作记忆。在交互过程中，决策所需的记忆内容会随智能体的状态、目标和任务进展而变化，同时许多内容在连续决策之间保持共享。然而，现有记忆模块通常通过相互独立的接口访问，导致每次更新的记忆上下文往往被当作全新输入交给基础模型处理。这使得系统无法对未变化的记忆内容进行选择性的键值（KV）缓存复用，即使大部分记忆上下文仍然有效，也必须进行完整的KV缓存重算。我们提出了HeMeR，一个在动态更新的记忆上下文与可复用KV状态之间执行KV协调的推理框架。HeMeR对声明性、程序性和工作记忆进行跟踪……
tldr: HeMeR提出了一种推理框架，通过在动态更新的异构记忆（声明性、程序性和工作记忆）上下文与可复用KV状态之间进行结构化协调，实现对未变化记忆内容的选择性KV缓存复用，避免不必要的完整KV重算，从而加速具身智能体的连续决策推理。
en_tdlr: HeMeR is an inference framework that reconciles dynamically updated heterogeneous memory contexts (declarative, procedural, and working memory) with reusable KV states, enabling structured KV cache reuse to eliminate redundant recomputation and accelerate embodied agents' sequential decision-making.
